newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa police storm hostage jail cells, one dead.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa police storm hostage jail cells, one dead.

text.p: One prisoner was killed and several were wounded on Wednesday when police and warders stormed cells where one of South Africa's most notorious criminals was holding five hostages, a prison spokesman said.

The action was taken after two days of negotiations failed to persuade Thembesile "Tyson" Makaluza to free the hostages he was holding in St Albans prison near the Indian Ocean city of Port Elizabeth.
"At 3 a.m. the police task force assisted by our members went into the prison and the hostage drama was then defused," prison spokesman Bert Slabbert told Reuters.
"The hostages are unharmed but one prisoner was shot and killed in the process and others were wounded. We will have more details later today," Slabbert added.
Makaluza, who is serving a 16-year sentence for armed robbery, shot and wounded two warders on Monday before taking five men hostage in a bid to break out of jail.
The hostages were three prison employees and two electricians who were carrying out repairs in the prison. They were referred to psychologists early on Wednesday following their ordeal.
State radio reported there were 55 other prisoners in the cells with Makaluza. One was killed and six were wounded in the shootout with police and guards, the radio said.
A full investigation into the hostage siege will now be carried out by the Department of Correctional Services.
Makaluza was due to appear in the Port Elizabeth high court later this month on charges which include robbery and 10 counts of murder.
